name: Georgia

notes: Food for home consumption, candy and soft drinks included, is exempt from the 4% state tax; local sales taxes apply to it, except that DeKalb County outside Atlanta charges 3% on food instead of its 4%.

Alcohol is taxed at the general rate. Cities and counties may add up to 3% on drinks with distilled spirits sold by the drink, on top of the sales tax (beer and wine aren't subject). It is counted on drinks with distilled spirits (43% of drinks served nationally, 2022 Economic Census) in the cities whose own forms or pages give the rate: Atlanta (Code 10-184), Brookhaven, Dunwoody, Johns Creek, Marietta, Sandy Springs, Savannah and South Fulton, all at 3% (local rates table). No list of the others that levy it was found (Athens-Clarke levies one but its page gives no rate), so elsewhere it isn't counted.
Cigarettes, other tobacco and vapor products are taxed at the general rate, on top of their excise taxes.
Barber and beauty services, and laundry and dry cleaning: not taxed (FTA 2017 survey answer).

Motor fuel is exempt from the 4% state sales tax. Local sales taxes are prepaid by distributors at each place's motor fuel rate, which leaves out its transportation SPLOST, on an average price the Department of Revenue sets ($3.00 a gallon for gasoline since July 1, 2026); those rates are used here. The state excise tax, left out here, is suspended from September 29 through November 30, 2026 (extended by the governor on October 24).
Repair labor is not taxed when it is billed separately from the parts.
Diapers and menstrual products are taxed at the general rate (a 2026 bill to exempt them from the state tax did not pass, as reported); clothing has had no sales tax holiday since 2016 (reported).

Hotel and motel stays carry local hotel taxes in about 310 cities and counties (2% to 8%; many at 8%, among them Atlanta, Savannah, DeKalb County, Columbus and Macon-Bibb) and a $5-a-night state fee, which this site does not count (Department of Community Affairs hotel-motel tax map, June 2025 edition; DOR).
Vehicles pay the title ad valorem tax instead of sales tax.

Georgia has no local tax on restaurant meals: the local sales taxes (LOST, SPLOST, ESPLOST, TSPLOST, MOST and MARTA) apply to them as to other sales and are counted (no other local meals tax was found, October 2026).
gaps: Georgia cities levy no general sales tax of their own except Atlanta, Hapeville, College Park and East Point (a municipal option sales tax, and in Atlanta also MARTA and a city transportation tax); the consolidated city-county governments' rate is the county rate, and every other city takes its county rate, so only places with their own rate are listed.

Other sales tax questions that passed on November 3, 2026 (Secretary of State, unofficial counts): SPLOSTs in Baker, Banks, Cherokee, Cobb, Jefferson, Lincoln, Marion, Oglethorpe, Seminole, Spalding, Talbot and Union counties; ESPLOSTs in Atkinson, Chattooga, Crisp, DeKalb, Emanuel, Quitman and Union; TSPLOSTs in Peach and Screven, whose motor fuel rates are 1% under their general rates (Department of Revenue), the gap a transportation sales tax leaves, so each looks like a renewal. Where each continues a current tax the rate stays the same; the Department of Revenue's 2027 rate charts will show any change. TSPLOSTs failed in Hart and Madison, whose motor fuel rates equal their general rates, so neither looks to levy one now.

Motor fuel carries each jurisdiction's motor fuel rate, which leaves out its transportation SPLOST, applied to an average price the Department of Revenue sets ($3.00 a gallon for gasoline since July 1, 2026) rather than the pump price.

1304000: In the Centennial Yards (the Gulch) and South Downtown enterprise zones, a 5% city infrastructure fee takes the place of the 4% state sales tax and the 1% local option sales tax, so buyers there pay the same 8.9% total; the zones aren't drawn separately here (Georgia Department of Revenue, bulletin SUT-2023-01; the South Downtown zone joined the state's rate chart October 1, 2026).

Atlanta's 3% tax on drinks with distilled spirits sold by the drink, on top of the sales tax, is counted in its rate for drinks served, on drinks with distilled spirits (43% of drinks served nationally, 2022 Economic Census; Atlanta Code 10-184).

13027: Brooks County voters approved a 1% property tax relief sales tax (FLOST) on November 3, 2026, 3,736 for and 1,608 against (Secretary of State, unofficial count). It raises the county's local rate from 4% to 5% once it starts; its start date wasn't read, and it is counted once the Department of Revenue's rate chart lists it. The current rate is used here.

It is counted once the Department of Revenue's rate chart lists it; the current rate is used here.

The FLOST is to run from January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2031 and raise the rate from 8% to 9% (Athens-Clarke County); it is counted once the Department of Revenue's rate chart lists it. The current rate is used here.
Athens-Clarke County levies a mixed drink excise tax on distilled spirits sold by the drink; its page gives no rate, so it isn't counted here (Athens-Clarke County excise tax payment page).

It wasn't the county's general SPLOST: voters continued that 1% for six years on May 19, 2026 (Resolution R-15-26; 1,564 for and 913 against, the county's unofficial election summary of May 19). Local 3 News reported the November question as a new 1% transportation sales tax from April 1, 2027; the county's own notice wasn't found. Dade's motor fuel rate equals its general rate (Department of Revenue), so no transportation sales tax is levied now, and the rejected question changes no rate. The FLOST is counted once the Department of Revenue's rate chart lists it; the current rate is used here.

Rates stay at 7.75% in the rest of Fulton County and 8.75% in Hapeville, East Point and College Park's Fulton County part (Fulton County).

tiers.label: Georgia job tax credit tier
tiers.what: Sets the per-job state income tax credit (O.C.G.A. 48-7-40; Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 560-7-8-.36): $3,500 a year for each new job in Tier 1, $2,500 in Tier 2, $1,250 in Tier 3 and $750 in Tier 4, with the fewest new jobs required in Tier 1 and the most in Tier 4; the 40 least developed counties are Tier 1.

programs: Atlanta's tax allocation districts are the eight Invest Atlanta lists (BeltLine, Campbellton Road, Eastside, Hollowell/Martin Luther King, Metropolitan Parkway, Perry Bolton, Stadium and Westside), from the City's map. That map also draws Atlantic Station and Princeton Lakes, which Invest Atlanta no longer lists, so they are left out. A plan to extend six of the TADs by 30 years passed the City Council in June 2026 over Fulton County's objection, as reported; its final status wasn't confirmed.

Tax allocation districts are also mapped for DeKalb County, Athens-Clarke, Macon-Bibb, Albany, Brunswick and Columbus (a 2016 parcel map, which doesn't show its Midland Commons TAD). No official map was found for Augusta's, Savannah's or Rome's TADs. Enterprise zones are mapped for Atlanta (Centennial Yards and South Downtown), Savannah and Columbus; the Department of Community Affairs keeps no statewide map, and Augusta's are shown only on the city's pages. Uptown Columbus' business improvement district isn't mapped.

Less developed census tracts are drawn from the Department of Community Affairs' 2026 map, which matches its 2026 list of 590 tracts except for three: the map has Chatham 108.11, Cobb 313.19 and Fulton 10.01 where the list has DeKalb 234.44, Floyd 12 and Muscogee 104.02.

warn.text: Taliaferro County may be flagged as a visitor economy only because the Census counts more than a quarter of its homes as seasonal or occasional-use homes; the county has no hotels or motels in the listing used here, so those homes may be hunting or weekend places rather than tourist rentals. Read that flag with care.
